summary: A thin day: Reddit, X and Bluesky were blocked from this environment, so every source below is a Hacker News comment checked against the live thread. Strongest themes were fear of losing Android sideloading, a wish for a light OneNote-style notes app that isn't Electron, parents wanting screen time without algorithmic feeds, and non-developers wanting a simple way to publish a site.

ideas.title: Sideload Vault
ideas.oneLiner: Android app that inventories every sideloaded app, keeps verified APK backups, and restores the whole set onto a new phone.
ideas.problem: A 540-point HN thread on Google's tightening of sideloading shows people who depend on APKs outside Play (open-source medical apps, privacy-focused setups) worrying about losing them. One commenter already hand-rolls the workflow: save every APK, rsync backups, reload on the next phone. Nothing packages that into a tool.
ideas.targetUsers: Privacy-minded Android users, GrapheneOS/F-Droid users, people running niche open-source apps such as insulin-pump controllers.
ideas.monetization: Free for up to 10 apps; one-time ₹399 / $5 unlock for unlimited apps, encrypted cloud/Nextcloud backup, and scheduled backups.
mvp: Scan installed packages and flag those not installed from Play
Save a copy of each APK plus SHA-256 and signing-certificate fingerprint
Export/import a backup bundle to local storage or a WebDAV/Nextcloud target
Guided restore onto a new phone, one app at a time
Per-app note showing where the app came from (GitHub, F-Droid, website)

competitors.name: Obtainium
competitors.gap: Tracks and updates apps from release pages, but is not built around backing up the APKs you already have and restoring the whole set to a new device.

competitors.name: F-Droid
competitors.gap: Only covers apps in its catalogue, not arbitrary APKs from GitHub or vendor sites.

sources.title: Your Phone Is About to Stop Being Yours: 70 Days Until Lockdown
sources.quote: I had "sideloaded" all the APKs for the software I used on the old phone and saved the APKs. Moving to a new phone was just a matter of loading all the software and copying my rsync'd backups onto the new phone. It was wonderful.

sources.title: Your Phone Is About to Stop Being Yours: 70 Days Until Lockdown
sources.quote: the absolute best app out there for controlling insulin pumps for diabetics is an open source app you have to "sideload."

sources.title: Your Phone Is About to Stop Being Yours: 70 Days Until Lockdown
sources.quote: As a long time iOS user, I just switched to GrapheneOS as the lack of sideloading, after 8 years, became too much pain.

ideas.title: Freeform Notes Lite
ideas.oneLiner: A fast, non-Electron, OneNote-style notes app with free placement and handwriting, built once in Flutter for desktop and tablet.
ideas.problem: People want OneNote-style free-form pages and handwriting, but say the open-source note apps are crowded and mostly Electron-based. They want something performant that matches OneNote's feature set.
ideas.targetUsers: Students and professionals who like OneNote's canvas, Linux and Mac users with no good OneNote client, tablet and stylus owners.
ideas.monetization: Free local use; paid sync/backup tier at about $3/month or a one-time license for the pro features.
mvp: Infinite page with free text boxes, images and ink
Pen input with palm rejection and pressure
Notebook > section > page tree stored as plain local files
PDF import and annotation
Fast startup and low memory use, as the main selling point

competitors.name: Saber
competitors.gap: Flutter, open source and handwriting-focused, but it is not a free-placement text-and-ink canvas like OneNote. These HN commenters still ask for one.

competitors.name: Microsoft OneNote
competitors.gap: The benchmark commenters cite; tied to Microsoft's ecosystem.

competitors.name: Obsidian
competitors.gap: Markdown-first, no free-form page placement or native handwriting.

sources.title: We should be more ambitious with the software we build
sources.quote: The note taking genre of opensource apps is saturated with many options but most of them are electron based. I was hoping that someone with enough motivation and money for tokens would come up with a non-electron option that is similar to onenote, with free form note placement and handwritten notes.

sources.title: We should be more ambitious with the software we build
sources.quote: I would be glad for a OneNote/Obsidian alternative that's performant.

ideas.title: Feedless Kids Player
ideas.oneLiner: A parent-curated tablet launcher that plays only approved videos and audio, offline, with no feed, search or autoplay.
ideas.problem: In a thread on Amazon's toddler tablet, working parents say screen time is sometimes unavoidable but argue a fixed movie is better than an algorithmic feed, and that locking down the open internet for kids is very hard.
ideas.targetUsers: Parents of children aged 2–8, especially dual-working parents and families on long trips.
ideas.monetization: Free for a small library; $20/year family plan for unlimited items, multiple child profiles and cloud sync of the library.
mvp: Parent adds videos or audio from local files or a home media server
Kid mode locks to the approved library with no search, feed or autoplay
Per-child daily time limit with a gentle end-of-session screen
Offline playback for travel
Parent PIN and an activity log

competitors.name: Amazon Kids+
competitors.gap: Ad-free, but a paid catalogue, with apps and games limited to Fire devices, and it is the product the thread was criticising.

sources.title: Amazon's "digital pacifier" for toddlers
sources.quote: I am a dual working parent. It is hard. I am not saying zero screen time. ... I think it's better to give them a movie rather than an algorithmic feed.

sources.title: Amazon's "digital pacifier" for toddlers
sources.quote: My wife and I are working parents. This is nightmarish. We know screen kids and they are not good around other people.

ideas.title: One-Page Site Publisher
ideas.oneLiner: A no-config site maker that turns a simple editor into a hosted static site in one click, for people who have no need for WordPress.
ideas.problem: Commenters ask why there is no easy GUI tool for making a website, and builders describe getting tired of wrestling with WordPress for a very simple task. Facebook's new paid link limits pushed people to want a site of their own.
ideas.targetUsers: Small businesses, creators and community pages leaving social platforms; non-developers who only need a page or a small blog.
ideas.monetization: Free subdomain; $4/month for a custom domain, analytics and more pages.
mvp: Pick a template and edit text and images in place
One-click publish to a static host
Custom-domain wizard with plain-language DNS steps
Simple blog or link-list page type
Export the site as plain files

competitors.name: Publii
competitors.gap: A free desktop static-site CMS, so the 'no GUI app' complaint is not fully true. It behaves like a full CMS, which is more than a one-page site needs.

competitors.name: Carrd / Wix
competitors.gap: Hosted builders with lock-in and paid tiers; users in these threads are asking for something simpler and more portable.
